A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSVQ work. All main-text and supplementary pages, including figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision quantization experiments, sign/freezing ablations and hardware simulations, with additional image-generation results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Llama3.2-1B evaluations and initial clustering-error comparisons.

M1.justification: v2 introduces Hessian-weighted k-means initialization for the Llama3.2-1B adaptation (Sections 5.3 and 11), while explicitly retaining ordinary k-means for vision experiments. The sign-splitting representation, joint sign/codebook optimization and Algorithm 1 freezing procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond vision to language modeling and zero-shot language tasks: Table 7 evaluates Llama3.2-1B on Wiki2, C4, WinoG, ArcE and ArcC. The earlier classification, detection, segmentation and image-generation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: VOC Table 4 adds a full-precision comparator with 72.9 mIoU. Table 6 drops the separately reported COCO2014 full-precision reference. Quantized comparator families are retained; NME becomes EMF but cites the same work, so this is a renaming.

E3.justification: The new NLP evaluation uses 2 and 2.5 bits per weight, perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. The new clustering analysis measures initial SSE across compression ratios. Existing vision training budgets and generation sample counts are retained; the added k/d tables primarily disclose settings rather than establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: New supplementary Section 9 and Figure 9 compare initial clustering errors on EfficientNet and DeiT-tiny, testing whether errors remain comparable after accounting for sign storage. Section 11 also reports a qualitative comparison of Hessian-weighted and ordinary initialization. Existing sign/freezing ablations and generation examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The six randomly sampled weight-position traces in Figure 4 are retained and do not constitute new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds NLP outcomes and initial-error curves; for example, Table 7 reports 2-bit Wiki2 perplexities of 63.1 for VQ and 13.9 for SSVQ. Existing diffusion values also change: Table 6 SD3 COCO FID-to-FP changes from 16.8 to 18.5 for VQ and 12.8 to 11.2 for SSVQ. Supplementary similarity scores are revised, including SDv2.1 COCO SSVQ PSNR from 13.3 to 13.8. The PDFs do not explain these numerical revisions.

T1.justification: v2 adds a Hessian-weighted clustering derivation with small-perturbation, convergence and diagonal-Hessian assumptions (Section 11, Equations 10–12). Its loss-difference definition and positive quadratic approximation have inconsistent signs for expansion around the pretrained weights. Conversely, v1's decoder bandwidth/parallelism condition (Equation 9) is removed. The relocated compression-ratio formulas retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: learnable sign splitting, enhanced iterative freezing, improved compression–accuracy trade-offs and a simulated 3× inference speedup. The additional NLP evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: New Section 11 qualifies the applicability of Hessian-weighted initialization: it reportedly benefits LLMs but provides no clear advantage on vision tasks, especially after fine-tuning, motivating ordinary k-means there. Existing interpretations concerning gradient dominance, sign oscillations, dimensionality and generation artifacts are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link and extensive k/d, compression-ratio and bit-accounting information in Tables 10–12, filling important documentation gaps in v1. Table 14 also corrects the duplicated DeiT-tiny label to DeiT-Small. However, Section 6.2 removes the multiport register-file implementation and two-codebook/four-read-port details, and NLP training details remain limited.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works covering DeepLab, DynamicID, SqueezeLLM, ConvNeXt, latent diffusion and DeiT. SqueezeLLM supports the Hessian-weighted initialization discussion; the other additions mainly supply background citations. The related-work positioning against existing VQ methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the preliminaries and portions of the method explanation, consolidates storage analysis into Section 5.1, and organizes additional appendix sections. It also corrects terminology and typographical errors, renames the sign initialization constant and adds acknowledgements. The overall narrative and most existing discussion are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the NLP table, clustering-error figure and three quantization-settings tables. It adds or reformats full-precision references in Tables 3, 4 and 6 and relocates several displays. Existing diagrams, performance curves, hardware plots and generated-image examples are retained, with local resizing, caption edits and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added quantization settings and code-access link improve reproducibility, while Figure 9 tests a previously asserted clustering premise and Table 7 broadens empirical support beyond vision. These gains outweigh limited losses of hardware documentation. Incomplete NLP training details and the sign inconsistency in the new Hessian derivation temper the improvement; the core method and most established evidence remain stable.
